teach.goal: Abrir a aula: objetivo e primeira hipótese.

Peça que cada aluno diga, em português, quando precisaria disso na vida real.

Peça um palpite sobre o que acontece na cena antes de abrir o diálogo.

facts.label: That depois de everything
facts.sub: Use that depois de everything, something, anything e nothing: everything that you need, something that is sweet. O verbo vem logo depois quando that é o sujeito.

facts.label: Tudo que
facts.sub: Use that depois de everything: everything that you need. Mantenha o verbo logo depois: everything that costs less, everything that looks fresh.

facts.label: Algo que
facts.sub: Use that depois de something para descrever o que você quer: something that is soft and white. É muito comum em compras e pedidos.

compare.ask: I have everything that I need.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “tudo que você precisa”, com “que” depois de tudo.
compare.tip: Diga: “I have everything that I need.”
compare.us: Em inglês, depois de everything, something, anything e nothing, use that: everything that you need.

pages.title: The supermarket · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a rainy Thursday evening in Seattle. A big supermarket is full of shoppers. Dee pushes a cart down the first aisle. Her friend Clara reads a long list. They are planning a dinner for six people. Dee wants to know what they still need.

“Clara, do you have everything that you need for the dinner?” says Dee. “Almost. I have everything that the recipe asks for, except the cheese.” says Clara. “Is there anything that I can pick up from aisle five?” says Dee.
